PACKAGES

One package (P-7) stops the run before the engineer: the test designer measured that the kernel template's form without the `PYTHONPATH` prefix cannot run three hook programs in a case where the prefixed form can. Nothing is built yet; the hooks source is unchanged.

## State of the branch

- **Head:** `a44c7b95` on `w1/W1-15`, tree clean, two commits on top of `w1/integrate` (`08b963e4`), no merge.
- **`68ccb44b`** (test designer): `Task: DAEO-7nne`, `Role: independent-test-designer`, `Implements: CAP-52.a`, `Co-Authored-By` — all present, checked when it appeared. Three files under `tests/acceptance/W1-38/`: the README, `w1_38_hooks_support.py`, and the new `test_w1_38_hooks_any_folder.py`.
- **`a44c7b95`** (mine): `Task: DAEO-7nne`, `Role: orchestrator`, `Implements: CAP-52.a`. It holds the checkpoint record `docs/checkpoints/DAEO-7nne/CP-DAEO-7nne-0005.md`; `gov checkpoint` answered `ok: true`.
- **Red, checked by me:** W1-38 to its end gives `31 failed, 114 passed`, no skips. All 31 fail because the generated command names its program by a relative path and the interpreter answers "can't open file" with exit 2.
- **Not run:** engineer, the other suites, unit tests, the whole of `tests/`, the validator, `gov check`. No reviewer was commissioned, as ordered.

## Package P-7 — the `PYTHONPATH` prefix of the seven command lines

**Question.** Do the seven command lines lose the prefix `PYTHONPATH="$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/src"` (the kernel template's form exactly), or keep it in front of the kernel template's path?

**Why now.** DEC-607 settles the prefix by the kernel template's form and orders a measured difference returned, not chosen. The engineer's seven strings and two of the designer's behaviours depend on the answer.

**Measured** by the designer, in four temporary projects generated from the template, each of the seven commands run from the root in both forms:

| Project | With the prefix | Without it |
|---|---|---|
| A. no `gov` under `src`, `gov` installed | all seven run | all seven run, same answers |
| B. `gov` under its own `src`, none installed | all seven run | `pretooluse.py` exits 2 at every call; `posttooluse.py` exits 2 ("No module named 'gov'"); `stop.py` writes no checkpoint |
| C. a product's own package named `gov` under `src`, `gov` installed | guard and containment exit 2, no stop checkpoint | all run |
| D. no `gov` anywhere | guard and containment exit 2 | the same |

- B fails closed, not open: every call is blocked.
- B is the shape of this repository and a clone of it; a product made from the template is A.
- In B, `sessionstart.py` and `precompact.py` still answer without the prefix. I read the template's programs: those two add the project's `src` to the import path themselves; `pretooluse.py`, `posttooluse.py` and `stop.py` do not.
- I did not re-run the four-project measurement myself.

**Options.**
- **(a) No prefix.** The kernel template's form exactly. A project needs `gov` installed for whoever runs its sessions. C is repaired, which removes DEC-601's named residual. B without an installed `gov` is blocked at every call.
- **(b) The prefix stays in front of the `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` path.** Hooks start from any folder and B runs. C stays DEC-601's residual. The agreement case compares the command line without the prefix.
- **(c) As (a), and the three programs that do not add the project's `src` look there after the installed package.** Both B and C run. It changes three programs under `template/governance/kernel/hooks/`, which are outside this ticket's paths and outside the owner's "no wider".

**Impact.**
- (a): the adopted dev-tier clone of your measurement, any CI runner and any other machine need `gov` installed for the user. DEC-605 did that on this machine only. The adoption notes gain the line "`gov` must be installed for the user who runs the project's sessions".
- (b): nothing changes for B; C stays as today.
- (c): the kernel's hook programs and their suites (W1-02, W1-05, W1-47).

**Reversibility.** High for (a) and (b): seven strings and a few cases. Medium for (c).

**Cost.** (a) or (b) is one short designer addition, then the engineer's seven strings and the verification. That designer addition is a second designer pass inside this run; whether it counts within DEC-584's "one run" is yours to say. (c) is a round of its own.

**Recommendation: (a).** It is what DEC-603 and DEC-607 word, the kernel template's own settings already work this way, it fails closed and loudly where `gov` is missing, and it removes residual C. Confidence: medium. The open point is whether any project of shape B is meant to run sessions without an installed `gov` (this repository under its own generated settings on a fresh machine or in CI).

## Cases so far

- **Added: 40**, all in `test_w1_38_hooks_any_folder.py`. Rewritten: 0. Removed: 0. The last round's 18 cases are unchanged and green.
- 28 hold each of the seven entries from the root, a subfolder, a deep subfolder and a folder outside the project: 21 red, the 7 root ones green.
- 7 hold a project folder with a space in its name: red.
- 3 hold a whole Bash call from a subfolder (out-of-scope change after a failed command reported, ordinary call not blocked, refused call refused by the guard's own answer): red.
- 2 keep the reading honest: green.
- **No case yet** for the command line agreeing with the kernel template's settings, or for a product package named `gov` no longer silencing containment. Both wait on P-7.
- The designer ran the new file and the last round's file against throwaway forms in the temporary project's copy only: 58 passed with the kernel template's form and also with the kernel path behind the prefix. So the 40 cases do not choose between (a) and (b).

## What can still be done meanwhile

Nothing in this run without the answer: the only implementation is the seven strings. After the answer, the order is the designer addition, a checkpoint, the engineer, a checkpoint, then the full verification.

## Residuals (not work)

- `program_of` in `w1_38_hooks_support.py` returns none for `subagentstop.py`, because `stop.py` is contained in its name; nothing compares that entry through it today.
- No case anywhere holds this repository's own rulesync hooks source equal to the template's (designer's search over `tests/`).
- The brief's `PATH=$HOME/...:$PATH` prefix breaks unquoted on this machine, whose `PATH` holds spaces; the quoted form works.
- During the designer's run, containment attributed its three test files to my waiting calls ("outside allowed paths, left in place"): a record of a permitted action under DEC-254.
- The README's package P-6 is marked answered by DEC-603, with the whole-command-line comparison waiting on P-7.
